voiceover:
[conversational] This boring database of investors makes about $25K a month.

And the fix that got it unstuck is something you can check on your own site today.

[curious] It's called Angel Match. A database of 125,000+ angels and VCs, with emails, outreach and pitch deck hosting. Founders raising money pay for it. Plans start at $59 a month.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR: about $25K MRR, $23K in the last 30 days, 320 active subscriptions, and almost $993K all-time. Revenue, not profit, and it's below the peak the founder once posted.

The founder, Rashid Khasanov, built it after his first startup failed. He'd struggled to find investors, so he started by collecting 600 to 700 of them by hand.

Growth was mostly SEO. Programmatic SEO pages got 6.34K clicks, blogs got 1.42K. He also made "Angel Match versus competitor" pages, because people searching for alternatives are ready to buy.

[whispers] So, the fix. It sat at about $5K for a long time, until an SEO expert came in. One summary says old pages kept getting deleted whenever the app updated, so search authority never built up.

[playful] Would you build a database business like this?

Send this to the friend who's raising a seed round.

Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Angel Match — Angel Match is a database of 124,000 angels and VCs to raise your seed round.

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Angel Match — Angel Match is a database of 124,000 angels and VCs to raise your seed round.
pick.angle: A simple database of 124,000 angels and VCs is making about $25K/month, selling to founders who are raising money

research.what_it_does: A searchable database of 125,000+ angel investors and VCs, with contact details plus built-in email outreach, an investor CRM, and pitch deck hosting, for founders raising a round.
research.who_pays: Startup founders raising capital (B2B subscribers). TrustMRR shows 320 active subscriptions.
research.pricing: Per third-party reviews of the pricing page (October 2026): Basic $59/mo, Growth $99/mo, Premium $349/mo at the default 2,000-investor tier. Every plan has a 3-day free trial, there is no free plan, and there are monthly and yearly options. Angel Match's own PitchBook comparison page confirms plans start at $59/month with a 3-day free trial. I could not load the pricing page itself, so check the live prices before filming. Older third-party listings show outdated prices ($99/$169/$299, or $59/$99/$199).
growth: SEO is the main channel. In his Indie Hackers/Starter Story write-up, Rashid says most users come from organic traffic and calls SEO the winner by far (source: starterstory.com/businesses/angel-match/growth-channels).

The same write-up says Angel Match sat at about $5k MRR for a long time, until they brought in an SEO expert (starterstory.com growth-channels; nocodeexits.substack.com). A Chinese-language summary of the Indie Hackers interview says the cause was that old pages kept getting deleted when the app was updated, so search authority never built up. That is a secondary source.

Programmatic SEO is the standout tactic. Starter Story's growth page quotes clicks by content type: Blogs 1.42K, Free tools 1.65K, Programmatic SEO resources 6.34K. Rashid posted on X that he doubts they'd have reached $20K MRR without pSEO, because it drives high-intent buyers (x.com/Rashidkhasanov, post dated Aug 5, year not shown).
A Startup Finder write-up says the SEO-first approach took Angel Match from $3,000 MRR to $20,000 MRR, and that Meta ads were layered on later (startupfinder.co).

Free tools and Product Hunt launches added to this. Angel Match 2.0 launched on Product Hunt on August 4th, 2021, with 241 upvotes, finishing #9 (hunted by Rashid, via hunted.space). Product Hunt lists Angel Match 4.0 as launched on May 28th, 2026. Indie Hackers shows a Jan 11, 2026 post: "We are trending #4 on Product Hunt today."
Free tools include a funding goal calculator at angelmatch.io/resources/funding-goal-calculator and an Investor Matcher launched May 15, 2026 (Indie Hackers).

Rashid posted on X that a paying user told him they had switched from a competitor. That gave him the idea for "angelmatch vs competitor" pages, because people searching for alternatives are high-intent buyers. He said the pages were created 2 days earlier and were already bringing in traffic (the post is cut off, and the year is not shown).
Facebook/Meta ads came later: Starter Story quotes the team saying most growth came from SEO and that Facebook ads were in early stages.
founder_story: Rashid Khasanov's first startup, a fintech app, failed. Indie Hackers says he drained his savings and maxed out his credit cards. While raising money for it, he found that finding investors was manual, painful work, and Angel Match grew out of that.

He began with 600 to 700 investor entries collected by hand. Over years this grew into a curated database of 110,000+ records (nocodeexits.substack.com), and Angel Match 4.0 (May 28, 2026) lists 125,000.

Not solo: Crunchbase lists Daria Ree as co-founder with Rashid, and Tracxn shows an employee count of 5 as of Jul 31, 2026. Product Hunt lists several makers. Tracxn also describes the company as unfunded, though another Tracxn FAQ line refers to a funding round, so that is inconsistent.
Rashid runs a portfolio: Angel Match, Investor Hunt, Journalist Hunt, Pur Social/autoposts. His X bio reads 'Building a portfolio of SaaS' (Indie Hackers, X).
Indie Hackers lists Angel Match as Bootstrapped & Active. TrustMRR gives the founding date as January 2019, matching Product Hunt ('Launched in 2019'). Tracxn says 2018.
lessons: Build for a pain you've lived. Rashid built Angel Match after struggling to find investors for his failed startup.
Data is a moat. A hand-built investor database is hard to copy quickly, and the founder frames it as something AI can't just generate.
Make SEO the core channel for a database product. Programmatic SEO pages drove 6.34K clicks, far more than blogs (1.42K) or free tools (1.65K) in the figures Starter Story quotes.
Check your own site for self-inflicted SEO damage. The reported stall at ~$5K MRR was linked to deleted pages, and an SEO expert spotted it.
Build 'vs competitor' and 'alternative' pages for high-intent searchers. Rashid got the idea from a customer who had switched, and angelmatch.io/alternatives/pitchbook is a live example.
Talk to paying users. Rashid posted that a user of 2+ years gave feedback he'd never thought of, and that they would now build what users want.
criticism: Revenue isn't profit. TrustMRR shows revenue only, and I found no verified profit or cost figures.

MRR is well below the peak Rashid himself reported. He posted about $43K/month and said they were now at $25K (X, Aug 4–5, year not shown), and Indie Hackers had $37K MRR about a year ago. TrustMRR now shows $24,804. Angel Match's own growth also looks volatile. A 10-day-old TrustMRR snapshot showed MRR of $27,098, higher than today's figure. That conflicts with the +15% MoM in the data given.

Competition: Round Funded, Angels Partners and PitchBook are listed as alternatives. Round Funded and Angels Partners position themselves against Angel Match, so treat their claims as competitor content.

Review sites say the database size is self-reported and not independently verified, there are zero reviews on Trustpilot, G2 or Capterra, there is no free plan, and email sends are capped by tier (from 100/month on Basic). These come from a competitor's review page (angelspartners.com), so treat them as partly biased.
Heavy reliance on organic search. A Google algorithm change could hurt it. This is my inference, not a sourced claim.
facts: TrustMRR (Stripe-verified): MRR $24,804, revenue last 30 days $23,799, all-time revenue $993,534, 320 active subscriptions, ranked #128.

Angel Match 4.0 (May 28, 2026) grew the database from 110,000 to 125,000 angels and VCs, and verified emails from 70,000 to 99,000+. It added email open/click/reply tracking and an inbox, and follow-up email flows (Indie Hackers).
Pitch Deck Hosting tool launched inside Angel Match on July 9, 2026 (Indie Hackers).
Per the Startup Finder write-up, trial conversion rate is 33.3% and the site pulls 800–1,000 clicks a day. This is founder-reported, and the page's date is unknown.
Angel Match's PitchBook comparison page says that PitchBook doesn't publish prices and that buyers report a median of $30,000/year. This is Angel Match's own marketing claim.
The founder's X audience is small (1,825 followers per TrustMRR), so the growth wasn't driven by a big social following.
do_not_claim: Exact team size (Tracxn says 5 as of Jul 31, 2026; other sources vary)
That the investor data is independently verified or 'accurate'
Funding: it appears bootstrapped, but there's no authoritative confirmation
Which year exactly the $43K-to-$25K decline happened
Exact customer counts beyond TrustMRR's 320 subscriptions
That the founder is 'non-technical' or hired a remote dev (only a Chinese secondary source says so)
Any claim that angel investor outreach through it actually leads to funding
research.notes: Pricing page URL: I'm confident angelmatch.io has a pricing page (its own pages link to it), but I did not load it, so the exact URL and whether '$59' is displayed are unconfirmed. The pitchbook and investor-match URLs appeared in search results, while the exact text to highlight on those pages is my best guess, so check each on screen before recording. The '$59' text IS confirmed on the PitchBook comparison page ('Plans start at $59 a month'), so use that page for a guaranteed highlight. Hook idea: a founder whose first startup failed, then built a spreadsheet of investors by hand into a ~$25K MRR business. The stuck-at-$5K-MRR SEO story is the best 'lesson' beat. Use the Indie Hackers MRR figures ($37K-$42K) only as the founder's earlier peak, not as current. Say 'about $25K MRR' using TrustMRR.
